## Intent
Hypothesis: delegating the Halide-expressible math+decide loop to Halide-generated code can approach the streaming ceiling on death-free workloads, with the host-scan mask loop adding proportional overhead at higher churn.

## Cache saturation
The L1d spill (N≈949) falls below the smallest measured point (N=10000), so every sample resides in L2 or beyond. At q=0.01, cost FALLS from 7.518 ns/p (N=10000, in L2) to 6.341 ns/p (N=10000000, DRAM) — pure overhead amortization with no knee at the L2→DRAM spill (N≈60787). At q=0.1 the curve is flat near 7.2 ns/p through N=100000 then RISES to 7.956 at N=1000000. At q=0.25 and q=0.5 the curve is FLAT across all N (8.3–8.6 and 10.5–11.0 ns/p respectively). Death rate raises the floor without reshaping the N-curve; no cache-spill knee appears at any churn level.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved is 10.88 GB/s at N=10000000, q=0.01 — 36% of the 29.9 GB/s streaming ceiling. At q=0.5 the peak drops to 6.56 GB/s (22% of ceiling). The algo is overhead/compute-bound, not bandwidth-bound: it never approaches the streaming ceiling in any regime. Bandwidth degrades with death rate (10.88→8.68→8.05→6.26 GB/s at N=10000000 as q rises 0.01→0.5), driven by the branchy respawn path rather than by N. There is no N-regime transition toward ceiling.

## Assembly
The histogram reports zero vector-suffixed instructions. The per-particle math inside `step` is entirely scalar: `ldp s5, s6`, `ldr s17`, `fcmp`, `fcvtzs`, `csel`, `fmul`, `fadd`, `fsub` on single-precision `s` registers — no `fmul.4s` or `ldr q` in the compute path. The only SIMD is `ldp q1, q0` + `orr.16b` + `ext.16b` in the mask-scan prologue, used solely to fast-skip empty 32-byte chunks, not to vectorize computation. The scatter is byte-granular (`strb w2, [x1]`, `strb w2, [x1, #0x1]`, `strb w2, [x1, #0x2]`), and loop2 issues 34 `bl` calls to `spawn` gated by per-byte `ldrb`/`cbz`. The scalar codegen and byte stores explain the 36% ceiling cap; the branchy respawn explains the death-rate sensitivity.

## Verdict
Refuted — peak bandwidth is 10.88 GB/s = 36% of the 29.9 GB/s ceiling at q=0.01, N=10000000, falling to 6.26 GB/s (21%) at q=0.5. The compiler emitted zero vector instructions; per-particle math runs on scalar `s` registers and the scatter uses byte-granular `strb`, so the mask-intermediate approach cannot approach the streaming ceiling regardless of death rate.
